stances_toward.note: Traore accused Abidjan of welcoming Burkina's destabilisers in April 2024. In April 2025 the junta announced a foiled plot it blamed on masterminds in Ivory Coast (junta claim, AFP copy); in September 2025 the head of state named neighbouring countries, Ivory Coast among them. Rival is our reading (C): friction and mutual charges, with no sign of a will to destroy the other regime; no source uses the word. Abidjan rejects the charges and says Burkina has offered no proof. Trend cooling from the 2024 to 2025 escalation. Bond grievance is our reading (the accusations and the detentions as an open wound). Gaps: the six Ivorian officials reported detained in late August 2025 come from search summaries and are not confirmed at source (the allAfrica article returned HTTP 403); JNIM attacks on the northern border are not sourced here.

stances_toward.note: Cooperation out of necessity under strain. Reluctant partner is our reading (C): relations soured after the 2022 coup and the December 2022 summons, yet security cooperation tightened after the 14 February 2026 Titao attack that killed Ghanaian traders (AFP). The necessity is the JNIM spillover across a porous northern border. The resisting-alignment half is not sourced here. Trend warming is our reading: seven instruments signed in February 2026 and boundary talks in June 2026, against the strain of 2022-25. Bond none: the index notes Sankara-era closeness, which is historical; no current kinship or grievance is documented. Sources are press and advocacy analysis, not official statements.

relations_to.summary: JNIM attacks in northern Benin rose sharply in 2025: an 8 January assault on the Point Triple base killed at least 28 soldiers and an attack on 17 April killed at least 54 (government toll, as reported). ACLED says JNIM uses Tapoa and Kompienga provinces in Burkina Faso as staging grounds for incursions into Benin. The Burkina state is not named as responsible; this row records the spillover, not a Burkinabe act.
relations_to.note: Counts differ by source (ADF Magazine reports 30 soldiers for January, ACLED 34). The 17 April toll is from a summary of the government's announcement, not opened.
